item.title: Holomorphic extremal surfaces for pseudoentropy in dS/CFT
item.description: arXiv:2610.24698v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We formulate the extremization problem for codimension-two hypersurfaces in de Sitter space in holomorphic coordinates, with real anchoring conditions at future infinity. The resulting equation ($K^I=0$) describes complex bulk realizations extending the usual piecewise Hartle--Hawking construction. We compute holographic pseudoentropy for harmonic deformations of spherical regions of arbitrary size and dimension, confirming its universal expansion through second order in the deformation parameter. The result is independent of the integration contour within each homology class on the complexified extremal surface. Inequivalent classes, labeled by an integer associated with a discrete global-coordinate isometry, differ by a sign of the universal term in odd boundary dimensions and by real finite shifts in even dimensions. For conical defects in dS$_3$ parametrized by a Schwarzschild-dS mass, we also verify the first law of pseudoentropy and the persistence of contour degeneracy within each homology class.
item.dc:creator: Giorgos Anastasiou, Ignacio J. Araya, Avijit Das, Javier Moreno

item.title: Complex spinodals and supercritical crossovers in Kerr-Newman-AdS$_4$ black holes
item.description: arXiv:2610.24978v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study supercritical crossovers in four-dimensional Kerr-Newman-AdS black holes at fixed angular momentum and charge. From the exact enthalpy, we prove uniqueness of the physical critical point and positivity of the quartic Landau coefficient throughout the charge-rotation family, treating the uncharged Kerr-AdS endpoint in separate scaling variables. An exact quartic reduction determines the coexistence entropies and latent heat throughout the subcritical regime. Above criticality, the two physical spinodals continue as a complex conjugate pair. Their real temperature projection defines a Widom-type line, and varying the charge-rotation ratio assembles these lines into a crossover surface. The Landau cusp fixes the imaginary entropy and temperature to scale with the square root and three-halves powers of the pressure displacement from criticality. The projected fold and the local heat capacity ridge share a critical tangent. We derive their leading quadratic temperature separation and prove that the ridge lies at a higher temperature near criticality. Exact endpoint solutions and numerical continuation check these predictions. The cusp exponents are common to the family, while the crossover temperature depends on the thermodynamic criterion used to define it.
item.dc:creator: Bum-Hoon Lee, Hocheol Lee, Somyadip Thakur

item.title: Beyond dust in local cosmography: perturbative Vlasov predictions
item.description: arXiv:2610.25145v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The dust approximation used in cosmography neglects the velocity dispersion generated during structure formation. This dispersion produces isotropic and anisotropic pressure, whose gradients accelerate the mean matter flow even though individual particles follow geodesics. The acceleration introduces an intrinsic dipole into the local distance-redshift relation. We calculate this dipole and the accompanying changes in expansion and shear using linear Vlasov perturbation theory about an FLRW background, with a mean dispersion history motivated by halo estimates. The assumed FLRW background prevents an independent test of the cosmological principle; the numerical predictions also depend on the adopted LCDM cosmology. Pressure also changes the growth of structure, modifying the shear and the spatial gradients that govern how the distance anisotropy varies with redshift. The largest correction at the lowest order in redshift is to the shear, while changes in the expansion gradient can produce a larger dipole at the next order. The resulting intrinsic dipole is far smaller than the observed low-redshift dipole, whose behaviour nearest the observer is dominated by motion between the matter and CMB frames.
item.dc:creator: Chris Clarkson, Roy Maartens

item.title: Lorentz-Invariance Violation with neutrinos from gamma-ray bursts using IceCube High-Energy Starting Events 12-year dataset
item.description: arXiv:2610.25214v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: High-energy astrophysical neutrinos provide a unique probe of Lorentz-invariance violation (LIV), as small energy-dependent deviations from the speed of light can produce measurable time delays over cosmological distances. We search for LIV-induced correlations between neutrinos and gamma-ray bursts using the public 12-year IceCube High-Energy Starting Event dataset and a catalog of 746 bursts with measured redshifts. We develop a likelihood analysis accounting for neutrino directional and energy uncertainties, a possible intrinsic time offset between neutrino and gamma-ray emission, and the decay of superluminal neutrinos expected within effective field theory. For linear LIV, the data show a mild preference over the background-only hypothesis, with a $p$-value of $3.1\%$, corresponding to a one-sided Gaussian significance of approximately $1.9\sigma$. The best fit corresponds to a LIV scale $\Lambda_{\rm LIV}=5.8\times10^{17}\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and is effectively driven by the subluminal component, as superluminal neutrinos are strongly suppressed by LIV-induced decays at the analyzed energies. The preferred LIV scale and the most significant neutrino--gamma-ray burst associations are consistent with previous studies based on different statistical approaches. No evidence for quadratic LIV is found. These results motivate further searches with complementary neutrino datasets, particularly at lower energies, where the superluminal component may become observable.
item.dc:creator: Mathieu Lamoureux, Jos\'e Manuel Carmona, Jos\'e Luis Cort\'es, Ardit Gkioni, Antoine Kouchner, Maykoll A. Reyes

item.title: $\Delta(1232)$ isobars and weak-interaction bulk viscosity in neutron-star merger matter
item.description: arXiv:2610.25224v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Binary neutron star mergers probe nuclear matter at densities of a few times nuclear saturation density and temperatures of tens of MeV, conditions under which heavier baryons such as the $\Delta(1232)$ isobars may appear. Previous calculations of the bulk viscosity of merger matter have considered nucleonic matter, with and without muons, and hyperonic matter, but not $\Delta$ isobars. In this work, we extend these calculations to neutrino-transparent matter in which $\Delta$ isobars are present in strong equilibrium. We derive the relativistic matrix elements for the charged-current $\Delta\to N$ and $\Delta\to\Delta'$ transitions, evaluate all electronic and muonic Urca processes over the full phase space using the nucleon width approximation, and include the in-medium $\Delta\to N\pi$ width with Pauli blocking. The bulk viscosity is obtained from the coupled linear response of the electron and muon fractions about the finite-temperature flavor equilibrium. We find that the $\Delta^-$ takes over the negative charge from the leptons, which raises the proton fraction and opens the nucleonic direct Urca process. Up to about 3~MeV this change in composition, rather than the $\Delta$ reactions themselves, controls flavor equilibration. As a consequence, the resonant maximum of the bulk viscosity moves to lower temperatures for all oscillation frequencies we consider, and kHz density oscillations near resonance are damped several times faster than in nucleonic matter. We also show that, for nucleonic matter, the choice of the equilibrium state about which the rates are linearized shifts the resonance temperature by up to a few MeV at high density.
item.dc:creator: Bharat Kumar

item.title: Squeezing and Decoherence of Axion Dark Matter
item.description: arXiv:2610.25466v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bosonic particles beyond the Standard Model, such as axions, are among the leading candidates for dark matter. If such particles have a small mass, they are usually described as a purely classical field. However, it was recently shown that this description is incomplete: their inherent gravitational self-interactions can squeeze the field, producing a quantum feature beyond the classical description. Here we analyze squeezing of light dark matter in the presence of decoherence. We show that squeezing is continuously generated, and rapidly enough to survive dissipation, and may also remain present under thermal fluctuations and dephasing. Our results demonstrate that dark matter might possess persistent quantum features and motivate further investigation of their implications for dark matter detection.
item.dc:creator: Vasileios Fragkos, Igor Pikovski

item.title: Closed locally symmetric spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2610.25542v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present some results concerning the geometry and dynamics of closed locally symmetric spacetimes.
item.dc:creator: Souheib Allout

item.title: Subsystem quantum R\'enyi-Bhattacharyya distance in 2D CFTs and its holographic applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.25685v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a systematic method to compute the subsystem fidelity and R\'enyi fidelity in two-dimensional conformal field theories (CFTs) from the operator product expansion of twist operators, and apply it to the subsystem quantum Bhattacharyya distance (BD) and R\'enyi-Bhattacharyya distance (RBD). We validate the method against exact results in the free massless fermion and boson theories, and then use it to compute the BD and RBD in holographic CFTs between two heavy primary states, between two thermal states, and between a heavy primary state and a thermal state. When the two states differ in their classical, order-$c$ data, the distances are of order $c$, and the states are distinguishable already at the level of classical gravity; when the leading data coincide, the distances are of order $1/c$ at every order of the short interval expansion, so that the distinguishability becomes a perturbative quantum gravity effect. For a heavy primary state and its thermal counterpart, the leading contribution to the BD appears at order $\ell^8$ and is of order $c^0$, whereas the RBD is generically of order $c$, in line with the earlier finding that a heavy primary state and a thermal state share the same order-$c$ entanglement entropy but have different order-$c$ R\'enyi entropies in the short interval expansion.
item.dc:creator: Yihao Wang, Jiaju Zhang

item.title: Hubble Susceptibility: Beyond Effective-Mass Spectroscopy in the Cosmological Collider
item.description: arXiv:2610.26014v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this note, we introduce the Hubble susceptibility of cosmological-collider masses, encoded in the scale dependence of the squeezed-limit oscillation. Heavy fields generically receive Hubble-induced mass corrections during inflation, and we show that the local oscillation frequency and its drift can disentangle such corrections from an intrinsic mass contribution at leading slow-roll and adiabatic order.
item.dc:creator: Shuntaro Aoki, Masahide Yamaguchi

item.title: The Geometry of the "Gauge Argument"
item.description: arXiv:2610.26049v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show how the "gauge argument", widely criticized by philosophers as ad hoc and unconvincing, may be reconstructed rigorously, and, we believe, convincingly, as an argument concerning the geometry of vector bundles. In this form, the gauge argument has two parts, the first of which is strongly analogous to the Weyl-Stein argument for Galilean spacetime as the appropriate setting for Newtonian gravitation; and the second of which invokes a classic result in the Yang-Mills theory literature, due to Utiyama [1956, "Invariant Theoretical Interpretation of Interaction", Phys. Rev. 101, 1597].
item.dc:creator: James Owen Weatherall, Benjamin H. Feintzeig

item.title: Gravitational Dark Matter Production in Einstein-Cartan Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.26237v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Introducing torsion into General Relativity leads to new four-point interactions for fermions. These are universal and must also affect any fermion dark matter. We improve existing calculations of dark matter production through the Einstein-Cartan theory four-fermion interaction by also considering the s-channel graviton exchange as another contributing process. The effect on both the total cross section as well as the momentum-dependent Boltzmann equation collision term is calculated and discussed. We also introduce the Holst term, which generally modifies the four-fermion interaction coupling constant as well as introduces two new four-fermion interactions, and discuss and compute its effect on the total produced dark matter abundance.
item.dc:creator: Kamil Mudrunka, Kazunori Nakayama

item.title: U(1) Current Diffusion in Gauss-Bonnet Holography
item.description: arXiv:2610.26515v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study holographic $U(1)$ charge transport using a probe Maxwell field in a five-dimensional Gauss-Bonnet-AdS black-brane background. Within the all-order linearised fluid/gravity framework, we derive the off-shell constitutive relation and determine the diffusion function and electric and magnetic conductivities analytically in the hydrodynamic regime and numerically at generic frequency and momentum. To first order in the Gauss-Bonnet coupling, the leading diffusion constant remains unchanged in our normalization, while its frequency dependence and the electric conductivity receive nontrivial corrections. The deformation also generates a nonvanishing leading magnetic conductivity. Beyond the hydrodynamic regime, it modifies the transport profiles while preserving the damped behaviour of the diffusion function. The corresponding memory kernel vanishes at negative times, supporting a retarded constitutive response.
item.dc:creator: A. Naveena Kumara, Shreyas Punacha, Kartheek Hegde

item.title: Mean-Field Backreaction in Single-Field Inflation
item.description: arXiv:2610.26669v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The validity of linear perturbation theory and the role of backreaction in single-field inflationary models that enhance power at small scales have recently been under debate. We investigate scalar backreaction semi-analytically in a mean-field approach within the decoupling limit, considering popular models with a transient ultra-slow-roll (USR) stage or an oscillatory feature (OF) in the potential. We find that ultraviolet (UV) modes in the Bunch--Davies vacuum can substantially affect backreaction estimates unless removed by adiabatic subtraction. Our mean-field treatment can reproduce recent lattice results, but reveals a spurious sensitivity to UV contributions in some cases. This sensitivity is reduced in the OF model when copious particle production separates the amplified physical modes from the UV vacuum tail, making lattice results more reliable in this regime. In USR, instead, adiabatically subtracted spectra yield milder backreaction on the background evolution than previously inferred.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Braglia, Gabriele Franciolini, Nadir Ijaz, Marco Peloso

item.title: Cosmological implications of two mock TianQin standard siren catalogs generated under different background cosmological models
item.description: arXiv:2610.26727v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Space-borne gravitational wave (GW) detectors such as TianQin are expected to detect GW standard sirens for cosmological parameter estimation. All previous studies of TianQin adopted the $\Lambda$CDM model to generate mock standard siren data. In this work, we quantitatively investigate how the choice of background cosmological model affects mock TianQin standard siren (TQSS) catalogs and the corresponding cosmological implications. Adopting the $\Lambda$CDM model and a redshift-binned dark energy (DE) reconstruction model (the wbin model), we consider the bright standard sirens from massive black hole binary mergers and generate two mock TQSS catalogs, i.e. TQSS1 and TQSS2, respectively. We investigate the difference of the catalogs and further explore their cosmological implications within the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) model, both individually and in combination with DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) data, $\textit{Planck}$ 2018 cosmic microwave background (CMB) data, and DESY5 type Ia supernova (SN Ia) data. We find that there are only small differences between TQSS1 and TQSS2 catalogs, with a maximum relative difference of $1.48\%$ in the distance-redshift relation. In addition, either the TQSS1 or TQSS2 catalog alone gives cosmological constraints similar to those obtained from SN data, implying that these two catalogs can serve as a complement to mainstream cosmological observations. Most importantly, we find that both TQSS1+DESI DR2+CMB+DESY5 and TQSS2+DESI DR2+CMB+DESY5 are still expected to favor dynamical DE, with these two combinations showing a preference for dynamical DE at $2.3\sigma$ and $3.8\sigma$, respectively. Adopting different massive black hole seed models does not impact the cosmological implications of the mock TQSS catalogs. Our study indicates the importance of considering different cosmological models in the standard siren forecasts for DE.
item.dc:creator: Jun-Xian Li, Shuang Wang, Liang-Gui Zhu

item.title: Mechanical angular momentum loss at $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ from static and radiative gravitons
item.description: arXiv:2610.26822v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the loss of mechanical angular momentum $L^{\mu}_{\rm loss}$ of two gravitationally scattering bodies at $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ using worldline quantum field theory (WQFT). The gravitational memory effect, a phenomenon of the early- and late-time behaviour of the gravitational field, leads to static contributions to $L^{\mu}_{\rm loss}$. We illuminate how these arise: the linear memory contributes through so-called static correlators, while the nonlinear memory vanishes at this order due to symmetry considerations. The computation of the remaining, dynamical part resembles that of the $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ impulse. We generate its integrand using a reformulation of the WQFT Feynman rules that conserves four-momentum at every vertex and plainly exhibits the classical loops. The three-loop integrals are reduced to master integrals, whose differential equations and boundary matching in the post-Newtonian limit we describe in some detail. In contrast to conservative effects at this order, only polylogarithms appear. While individual contributions to the dynamical part are divergent, these cancel in $L^{\mu}_{\rm loss}$. The quadratic-in-radiation part of our result reproduces earlier results, while the complete result agrees with existing post-Newtonian results.
item.dc:creator: Lara Bohnenblust, Carl Jordan Eriksen, Gustav Uhre Jakobsen, Kathrin Stoldt, Andrii Yanovets

item.title: On the geometry of quantum constrained systems
item.description: arXiv:0801.1119v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Geometric methods have proved useful in the Hamiltonian description of classical constrained systems. We develop the corresponding geometry for quantum constrained systems, using the formulation of quantum mechanics in which the space of rays $\Ps$ is a K\"ahler manifold and unitary transformations are its canonical transformations. The Dirac conditions $\hat C_i\Psi=0$ define the zero set of a single function $\Cq=\ev{\Mop}$, the expectation value of the master constraint operator. Our central identity is $\Cq=|\mu|^2+\tfrac12\|X_\mu\|^2$, where $\mu=(\ev{\hat C_i})$ is the moment map of the gauge action on $\Ps$ and $X_\mu$ its fundamental vector fields: the quantum condition imposes the classical-type condition $\mu=0$ \emph{and} the collapse of the gauge orbits to points. This explains why no second reduction is needed. The physical state space is a totally geodesic K\"ahler submanifold. $\Cq$ is a Morse--Bott function which gradient flow is heat-kernel-smeared group averaging, converges to the nearest-point projection onto physical states, and its fibres are invariant under the complexified gauge group. Physical observables are characterised to all orders by the double-commutator condition, which is equivalent to $[\hat O,\hat P_0]=0$, with $\hat P_0$ the projector onto physical states. When zero lies in the continuous spectrum, the gradient flow converges to Dirac states in the sense of Grundling and Hurst, and its large-time asymptotics reproduce the rigging map of refined algebraic quantization. Finally, pulled back along coherent states, $\Cq$ equals the classical master constraint plus an $O(\hbar)$ term given by the squared speed of the classical gauge orbits. Together these results connect the Dirac procedure, the master constraint programme, refined algebraic quantization and symplectic reduction within one geometric picture.
item.dc:creator: Alejandro Corichi

item.title: Improving Slow-Roll Estimates in Starobinsky Inflation Using an Analytic Hubble Parameter
item.description: arXiv:2307.01899v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Inflationary observables are naturally formulated in terms of the Hubble-flow hierarchy. Because exact background solutions are often unavailable, the Hubble-flow parameters are commonly approximated using potential slow-roll (PSR) quantities constructed from derivatives of the inflationary potential. We revisit the accuracy of this replacement for Starobinsky inflation by mapping analytic Jordan-frame background variables to their Einstein-frame counterparts and deriving the Hubble-flow parameters directly. The leading analytic background is an exact solution of a controlled deformation of the Starobinsky action. Linearizing the pure Starobinsky equation about this background yields a closed-form perturbative correction. Using the same first-order spectral expressions throughout, the perturbatively corrected background tracks the numerical evolution of the first two Hubble-flow parameters more accurately than the next-to-leading-order (NLO) PSR approximation over the common domain in which the NLO expressions remain physical. Moreover, the NLO estimate of \(\widetilde{\epsilon}_1\) reaches a maximum value of approximately \(0.114\), subsequently decreases, and therefore cannot determine the end of inflation from \(\widetilde{\epsilon}_1=1\). For the Planck 2018 central value \(n_s=0.9649\), the perturbatively corrected background gives \(\widetilde{N}_*\simeq55.60\), compared with \(55.72\) for the converged numerical background and \(56.98\) for the conventional large-\(\widetilde{N}_*\) estimate. For the adopted ACT DR6 combined-data value \(n_s=0.974\), it gives \(\widetilde{N}_*\simeq75.43\), compared with the conventional value \(76.92\). The analytic construction therefore provides a self-consistent endpoint and a first-order estimate of the e-fold number that closely reproduces the converged numerical result.
item.dc:creator: Jose Mathew

item.title: Unruh effect using Doppler shift method in DSR framework
item.description: arXiv:2403.20146v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Unruh effect in doubly special relativity (DSR) framework by generalising the Doppler-shift method to DSR. For both the scalar and Dirac particles, we observe a deviation in the power spectrum of Unruh radiation from the standard Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac distributions, respectively, due to the presence of the frame independent length scale of DSR. We further show that this deviation results in the modification of Unruh temperature which then depends non-linearly on the proper acceleration in DSR.
item.dc:creator: Vishnu Rajagopal

item.title: Kerr-Newman outside a rotating de Sitter-type core: Different types of interior electromagnetic fields and currents
item.description: arXiv:2407.01228v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the structure of interior electromagnetic fields compatible with the exterior Kerr-Newman geometry when regular interior geometries for describing regular black hole solutions are considered. Working within the G\"urses-G\"ursey framework and considering a rotating de Sitter-type geometry in the interior region, we analyze a particular class of electromagnetic fields aligned with the principal null directions and satisfying Maxwell electrodynamics. We show that, within such a class of interior electromagnetic fields, no well-behaved interior electromagnetic field can be supported in the absence of electromagnetic currents. Moreover, we show that for the same interior and exterior geometries, different types of interior electromagnetic fields and charge distributions, together with different charge densities on the rotating boundary shell, can be constructed while matching the same exterior Kerr-Newman electromagnetic field. This results highlight the non-uniqueness of the interior electromagnetic structure compatible with a given Kerr-Newman exterior. For a particular choice of interior electromagnetic fields we show that the de Sitter fluid can be interpreted as being electrically polarized by the rotating charged shell. In this case, the interior region contains no net electric charge, which is instead concentrated entirely on the shell, and the interior medium behaves as a perfect conductor with infinite conductivity. In a second choice for the electromagnetic field, we show that the polarized de Sitter fluid also contributes to the total electric charge, with the interior medium acting as a nonisotropic conductor.
item.dc:creator: Marcos L. W. Basso, Vilson T. Zanchin

item.title: Probing Compact Binary Coalescences in the Decihertz GW Band with IndIGO-D
item.description: arXiv:2601.06956v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present an astrophysical science-case study of IndIGO-D, a decihertz gravitational-wave mission concept, focusing on compact binary sources across the 0.1-10 Hz band bridging LISA and next-generation ground-based interferometers. For these science projections, we consider three spacecraft forming an L-shaped interferometer in a heliocentric orbit, with two orthogonal 1000 km arms sharing a common vertex. We calculate the time-dependent antenna response of this geometry, including modulation produced by the orbital motion of the constellation. We treat the strain-sensitivity curve supplied by the IndIGO-D collaboration as an input. For the assumed sensitivity, we estimate a BNS detection rate of $\sim76$-$767\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$. We compute horizon distances for different source classes and find that intermediate-mass black-hole binaries with masses $10^2$-$10^3\,M_\odot$ are detectable throughout their formation history, complementing the reach of LISA and terrestrial detectors. Binary neutron star systems are observable to a horizon redshift of $z\lesssim0.3$, allowing continuous multi-band coverage with Voyager-class interferometers from the decihertz regime to merger. A Bayesian parameter-estimation study of a GW170817-like binary shows that the sky localization area improves from $\sim21\,{\rm deg}^2$ at one month, $\sim1\,{\rm deg}^2$ at one week, down to $0.3\,{\rm deg}^2$ at six hours pre-merger. These sky areas are readily tiled by the Rubin Observatory, whose $9.6\,{\rm deg}^2$ field of view and r-band depth enable high-cadence, repeated coverage of GW170817-like kilonovae at this distance and beyond. IndIGO-D bridges the gap between millihertz and terrestrial observations, enabling early warnings on timescales from months to hours and enhancing the prospects for multi-band and multi-messenger discoveries. (abridged)
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Sharma, Divya Tahelyani, Anand S. Sengupta, Sanjit Mitra

item.title: Analog regular black holes and black hole mimickers for surface-gravity waves in fluids
item.description: arXiv:2604.08671v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent advances in the observation of black-hole candidates have renewed interest in probing their near-horizon structure and in searching for departures from the standard singular solutions of general relativity. In this context, significant effort has been devoted to regular black holes and to horizonless black-hole mimickers, motivated primarily by quantum-gravitational effects. Depending on the value of the regularization parameter relative to the object mass, typical spherically symmetric solutions can describe either of these two scenarios. Regular black-hole configurations generically feature an outer and an inner horizon surrounding a maximally symmetric core; the inner horizon in turn triggers mass inflation and semiclassical instabilities. The horizonless branch of the same solutions, by contrast, supports stable inner light rings when sufficiently compact, yet is itself subject to instabilities associated with long-lived quasinormal modes. Here we investigate how to emulate these spacetimes in an analogue-gravity platform based on surface-gravity waves in a shallow-water basin, with the aim of reproducing these instabilities experimentally. We begin by identifying the flow profiles and boundary conditions required to replicate the relevant effective geometries. In particular, we show that the inner-core metrics can be simulated with a non-rotating central-drainage configuration, and we propose a graded-drainage profile to connect them to an asymptotically flat exterior region. We then assess the experimental feasibility of studying the instabilities mentioned above with current technology. Our conclusion is that, while the required setup is realizable in principle, alternative media, such as Bose-Einstein condensates, may offer a more practical route to faithfully capturing the targeted physical features.
item.dc:creator: Valentin Pomakov, Stefano Liberati

item.title: Shadow of rotating black hole surrounded by dark matter
item.description: arXiv:2604.11822v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dark matter (DM), a fundamental cosmic component, motivates the study of its influence on black hole (BH) shadows, especially for spinning BHs confirmed by EHT observations. This work generalizes the Schwarzschild BH surrounded by DM to an axisymmetric Kerr BH using the Newman-Janis Algorithm (NJA), investigating the resulting event horizon and ergosphere structures. Employing null geodesics, we examine the effects of DM mass $\Delta M$ on BH shadow, including its radius, distortion, and the associated energy emission rate. Our analysis reveals that DM has a negligible effect below a critical mass, once this threshold is surpassed, all BH structures expand significantly. Furthermore, DM robustly contributes to the shadow maintaining a near circular shape, even for highly spinning BHs. This pronounced structural expansion under high DM mass may potentially exceed current observational constraints, suggesting that DM must either be absent in the immediate vicinity of the BH or its localized mass must remain below this critical value to be consistent with astrophysical observations.
item.dc:creator: Haiyuan Feng, Ziqiang Cai, Rong-Jia Yang, Jinjun Zhang

item.title: Quantum gravitational contrast in creating Schr\"odinger cat state
item.description: arXiv:2605.05153v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we illustrate how a Schr\"odinger cat state created via a matter-wave interferometer can be viewed as the simplest quantum-gravity setup where we can treat both matter and gravity on an equal footing at a perturbative level. Here we treat Einstein's theory of general relativity using an effective field theory approach, quantising the massless spin-2 graviton in the presence of a quantum spatial superposition of matter that creates a matter-wave interferometer in the non-relativistic limit. We show that, due to the matter-graviton coupling, the graviton vacuum is displaced analogous to the coherent state. We study the contrast/overlap between the coherent states of the left and right superpositions in the matter-wave interferometer. We also study the entanglement between matter and the graviton in this setup and relate it to a gravitational contrast, or the overlap of the quantum geometries led by the coherent states. In the appendix, we provide an example of a time-dependent harmonic oscillator and study the contrast/overlap of such coherent states of the graviton.
item.dc:creator: Anupam Mazumdar, Tian Zhou

item.title: Demagnetizing KBR and New Ricci-flat Rotating Metric
item.description: arXiv:2605.13954v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a new Ricci-flat metric by demagnetizing the recently reported Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson (KBR) solution. The metric is a deformation of the Kerr metric characterized by a parameter $B$, so that the asymptotic Kerr becomes a regular dome of spindle shape with north and south poles. Despite lacking an asymptotically-flat region, we find that the first law of black hole thermodynamics can be established. Some thermodynamic relations are identical to those of the Kerr black hole, as if the constant $B$ is absent. Our Ricci-flat rotating metric serves a neutral seed for a variety of inequivalent schemes of magnetizing the Schwarzschild and Kerr black holes.
item.dc:creator: Liang Ma, H. Lu

item.title: Static spherically symmetric Kundt vacuum solutions of higher-derivative gravities
item.description: arXiv:2605.14658v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study static spherically symmetric Kundt solutions to the vacuum field equations of quadratic gravity with a cosmological constant, as well as specific models of six-derivative gravity. In quadratic gravity, we identify all solutions for coupling constants satisfying ${\alpha\neq3\beta}$, while the case ${\alpha=3\beta}$ is studied using the Frobenius method, where we derive the recurrence relations for the power series. In contrast, in six-derivative gravity, we focus on selected models to illustrate the variety of closed-form solutions; we also analyze possible indicial families of Frobenius solutions. For all solutions, we analyze curvature singularities and their accessibility to geodesic observers. We then construct exact gravitational-wave solutions propagating on some of these backgrounds in quadratic and six-derivative gravity. It is known that in Einstein gravity, gravitational waves on the Nariai background unavoidably contain singularities, which are interpreted as physical sources generating these gravitational waves. In contrast, in addition to singular solutions, for appropriate values of the coupling constants, higher-order gravities allow for globally smooth solutions representing gravitational waves.
item.dc:creator: Breno L. Giacchini, Ivan Kol\'a\v{r}, Vojt\v{e}ch Pravda, Alena Pravdov\'a

item.title: Global curvature control in a regular black hole with Minkowski core and inner-extremal horizon
item.description: arXiv:2605.15576v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a static, spherically symmetric regular black hole with a Minkowski core, a non-extremal outer horizon, and a degenerate inner horizon with vanishing surface gravity. The spacetime exhibits two main features. First, in the large-mass regime with $r_+=2M$, the maximal Kretschmann scalar becomes nearly independent of the ADM mass and is mainly controlled by the inner-horizon radius $r_-$, providing a simple sufficient condition for the curvature to remain sub-Planckian everywhere. Second, the effective cubic zero of the metric function replaces the standard exponential near-horizon amplification with power-law behavior. A massless scalar test field shows that the geometric blueshift factor grows as $v^{3/2}$. Then, we use the double-null shell and Ori models to examine the corresponding effective mass dynamics. the nonlinear shell-crossing contribution decays at late times, while the Ori evolution with a Price-law ingoing flux keeps the internal Misner-Sharp mass bounded. In both descriptions, the late-time mass approaches $r_-/2$. The same inner-horizon scale therefore controls the global curvature bound and the finite mass scale reached by the shell dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Zhong-Wen Feng, Hong-Lin Liu, Yi Ling, Qing-Quan Jiang

item.title: Gravitational Wave Propagation in K-essence Cosmology: Theory and Observational Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2605.25466v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Gravitational waves (GWs) provide a powerful, theory-independent probe of the dynamical structure of spacetime and the cosmological background. We investigate the propagation of linearized tensor modes in k-essence cosmology, where the dark sector is described by a non-canonical scalar field. Working in the high-frequency (short-wavelength) limit on a Friedmann-Lema\^{\i}tre-Robertson-Walker background and restricting to the transverse-traceless sector, we obtain a modified evolution equation in which the GW speed remains strictly luminal (compatible with GW170817), while the background field $\bar{\phi}$ generates a time-dependent effective mass term $m_{\rm eff}$. This background-induced mass alters the dispersion relation without introducing extra propagating degrees of freedom, producing an accumulated, frequency-dependent phase shift over cosmological distances. We show that $m_{\rm eff}$ is uniquely determined by background cosmological parameters and can be expressed as a redshift-dependent function $m_{\rm eff}(z)$, providing a direct connection between GW observables and scalar-field dynamics. The GW luminosity distance stays identical to the electromagnetic one, preserving standard-siren consistency. We confront the model with a joint Bayesian analysis combining cosmic chronometers, BAO, Pantheon+SH0ES, and standard-siren measurements from GWTC-2.1/3/4, and assess performance using $\chi^2$, $\chi^2_{\rm red}$, AIC, BIC, and DIC. The reconstruction is consistent with current data, reproduces the late-time expansion history, and provides data-driven constraints on the redshift evolution of $m_{\rm eff}(z)$.
item.dc:creator: Sougata Bhunia, Goutam Manna, Eduardo Guendelman, Debashis Gangopadhyay, Ram\'on Herrera, Abhijit Bhattacharyya

item.title: Stochastic scalar-tensor inflation and beyond
item.description: arXiv:2606.07467v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: During cosmological inflation, inhomogeneities arising from quantum vacuum fluctuations are stretched to become super-Hubble and effectively classical. As many scenarios of the origin involve nonlinearities or a breakdown of perturbativity in the infrared, the limitations of quantum field theory can be addressed using a stochastic description of the dynamics, the so-called stochastic inflation paradigm. However, the stochastic formalism was only recently formulated consistently within full General Relativity and has not yet been extended to more general theories of the early universe, which is the subject of this work. In order to find the stochastic sources for a wide class of fully nonlinear scalar-tensor theories, we apply our gauge-agnostic coarse-graining procedure to the linear equations of the associated effective field theory. Each theory can then be mapped to its own set of stochastic equations of motion by identifying the corresponding coefficients in the former. We illustrate this with a few concrete and, in most cases, unprecedented examples, including Gauss-Bonnet, generalized Brans-Dicke, Horndeski, and braiding theories. Finally, we discuss other natural extensions to provide a phenomenologically complete stochastic framework. For example, we showcase the coarse-graining of multifield inflation in full General Relativity and argue for the generality of our procedure and thus its potential applications beyond the realm of inflation.
item.dc:creator: Yoann Launay

item.title: Self-stimulated avalanche in superradiant axion clouds
item.description: arXiv:2606.10776v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Boson clouds formed via superradiance around spinning black holes offer a novel probe of ultralight particles. We show that such gravitational atoms can undergo a self-stimulated avalanche: a coherent quadrupolar transition is seeded by external gravitational waves and amplified by self-generated radiation feedback. We formulate an effective two-level description that captures the logistic population transfer and the resulting delayed gravitational-wave pulse with a characteristic envelope. This cooperative emission mechanism opens a new observational avenue into the ultralight dark sector.
item.dc:creator: Zhen-Hong Lyu, Rong-Gen Cai, Jing Liu

item.title: SPLIT: Loosely-coherent inference of long-inspiral gravitational-wave sources for robustness against modeling and data outliers
item.description: arXiv:2606.13728v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will detect gravitational waves (GWs) from dozens of extreme- and intermediate-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs/IMRIs). These sources will stay in-band for months to years, offering extraordinary scientific potential. However, their fully phase-coherent analysis standard in current pipelines imposes stringent waveform accuracy requirements; failing to model the signal over such long durations can result in significant systematic biases. To address this, we formulate a robust Bayesian inference framework that segments the data into blocks, infers each block coherently, and recombines the results using loosely-coherent phase information. By restricting full phase-tracking to much shorter block durations, this approach prevents significant accumulation of phase errors. We implement this methodology in \textsc{SPLIT} (Segmented Posteriors for Long-Inspiral Templates), a GPU-accelerated Python package. Applying \textsc{SPLIT} to an environment-rich injection, we demonstrate that while a fully-coherent vacuum-GR analysis incurs a maximum 1D systematic bias of $\approx 4.8\sigma$ from the truth, the shorter integration window of our loosely-coherent approach restricts such biases to $\lesssim 0.5\sigma$. Overall, despite a fractional loss of optimal signal-to-noise ratio, the substantial improvement in parameter accuracy offered by our method presents a highly advantageous trade-off for LISA and other future GW detectors.
item.dc:creator: Shubham Kejriwal

item.title: Searching for Extra Dimensions with Gravitational Waves: Dark-Siren Constraints from GWTC-4
item.description: arXiv:2606.14549v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Higher-dimensional theories of gravity predict that gravitational waves (GWs) can propagate into extra spatial dimensions, leading to modified amplitude damping over cosmological distances. Measurements of GW luminosity distances therefore provide a unique probe of the dimensionality of spacetime. In this work, we constrain higher-dimensional GW propagation using the dark-siren method with the Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog 4.0 (GWTC-4). We adopt a phenomenological parameterization motivated by braneworld scenarios, in which deviations from General Relativity are characterized by the spacetime dimension number $D$ and a crossover scale $R_c$ governing the transition between four- and higher-dimensional gravity. We perform a hierarchical Bayesian analysis combining 141 compact binary coalescences from GWTC-4 with line-of-sight galaxy information from the GLADE+ catalog. For a prior $H_0 \in [65,77]\ {\rm km~s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$ and $\log(R_c/{\rm Mpc}) \in [2.7,4.0]$, we obtain $D = 4.38^{+1.91}_{-1.01}$ (68\% credible interval). We also find that the inferred posterior distribution of $R_c$ accumulates near the upper prior boundary, indicating that the crossover scale remains poorly constrained by current observations. We further show that the inferred constraint on $D$ depends sensitively on the assumed prior range of $R_c$, which determines the characteristic distance scale at which deviations from General Relativity become significant. Our results provide the first GWTC-4 dark-siren constraints on higher-dimensional GW propagation and demonstrate that current observations remain consistent with four-dimensional General Relativity.
item.dc:creator: Anson Chen, Jun Zhang

item.title: Regular Black Holes from Anisotropic Source with Hydrodynamic Equation of State
item.description: arXiv:2606.20109v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study regular black hole solutions sourced by an anisotropic energy momentum tensor. It is well known that the geometry of the interior of a spherically symmetric regular black hole approaches the dS metric. Having decomposed the energy momentum tensor into its isotropic and anisotropic components, we assume a hydrodynamic equation of state, $P= P(\rho)$, for the pressure, and look for spherically symmetric, regular black hole solutions. We consider different forms of $ P(\rho)$ which yield the previously known regular black hole solutions, as well as various new metrics. We show that the profile of $ P(\rho)$ has a root and a maximum as it approaches $0^+$ at large distances. Consequently, the square of the sound speed of perturbations, $c_s^2$, changes sign at the point where $P$ reaches its maximum, indicating a potential hydrodynamic instability. In addition, imposing the subluminal bound on $c_s$ puts strong constraints on the model parameters, excluding models in which the energy density has an exponential fall off. We establish a universal hierarchy among the relative positions at which the strong energy condition is violated, at which $P$ has its root, and at which $P$ attains its maximum.
item.dc:creator: Hassan Firouzjahi

item.title: Nanohertz gravitational waves from domain walls nucleated during inflation
item.description: arXiv:2606.24070v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) produced by domain walls (DWs) nucleated via quantum tunneling during inflation with an extended nucleation time. In contrast to the small-period nucleation framework, in which DWs form over a narrow interval and possess nearly identical radii, we show that an extended nucleation period leads to a distribution of DW radii characterized by $\gamma\equiv\overline{R^{10}}/(\overline{R^5})^2>1$, which enhances the resulting curvature perturbations. We construct a two-field inflation model with an inflaton $\phi$ and a spectator field $\chi$ coupled through the potential $V(\phi,\chi)$, where the DW tension $\sigma(t)$ evolves smoothly as the inflaton rolls past a critical value. The characteristic width of this transition determines the cutoff scale $k_{\text{cut}}$ of the curvature power spectrum, enabling the SIGW peak to be placed in the nanohertz frequency band with detectable amplitude. For three representative parameter sets, we compute the SIGW spectra and find that the peak frequency ranges from $\sim10^{-8}$\,Hz to $\sim10^{-1}$\,Hz, with the nanohertz-peaked spectrum matching the NANOGrav and EPTA signals for suitable parameter choices. By selecting different parameters, our model can produce signals detectable by different gravitational-wave detectors.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Yong Huang, Tie-Jun Gao

item.title: Quasinormal modes as probes of black hole reentrant phase transitions
item.description: arXiv:2606.29101v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the interplay between thermodynamic phase transitions and the dynamical behavior of quasi-normal modes (QNMs) in weakly nonlinear charged anti-de Sitter black holes. In a non-extended phase space, we identify a reentrant large-small-large(intermediate) phase transition for these black holes. Employing the shooting method to solve the Klein-Gordon equation for a massless scalar field, we compute QNM frequencies across these phases, revealing distinct behaviors in different phases. Specifically, to our knowledge, this is the first report of utilizing QNMs as dynamical probes of thermodynamic phases during reentrant phase transitions including zeroth and first-order transitions. These findings establish QNMs as a powerful dynamical probe for thermodynamic phase transitions, providing new insights into the thermodynamic and dynamical properties of nonlinear charged black holes as well.
item.dc:creator: M. Kord Zangeneh, S. Abdollahi, D. Afshar

item.title: Quasi-bound states and late-time evolution of a massive fermion around a Reissner-Nordstr\"{o}m black hole
item.description: arXiv:2607.08258v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A massive fermion around a charged black hole provides a gravitational analogue of atomic bound states and their relaxation. In this work, we study this system by formulating the radial equation as a coupled matrix system and constructing the Green's function with ingoing boundary conditions at the horizon and decaying boundary conditions at infinity. In the weak-coupling scenario $|qQ|\sim mM<1$, a matrix matching scheme gives an improved analytic expression of quasi-bound-state spectrum, including fine-structure corrections and more accurate decay widths. The extremal Reissner-Nordstr\"{o}m case ($|Q|=M$) is treated separately and shown to be the smooth limiting result of the non-extremal spectrum. We further analyze the branch-cut contribution to the time-domain Green's function in the late-time limit. We confirm an oscillatory power-law behavior in intermediate late-time regime $1/m < t < 1/m^3M^2$. In the far late-time regime $t>1/m^3M^2$, the activation of the quasi-bound states produces an $t^{-5/6}\exp(-\eta t^{1/3})$ suppression with a chirping phase before the asymptotic $t^{-5/6}$ tail previously found in the limit $t\to\infty$. Direct time-domain simulations support this distinction and show how the quasi-bound contribution coexists with the familiar power-law component.
item.dc:creator: Guang-Shang Chen, Cheng-Bo Yang, Shou-Shan Bao, Yue-Liang Wu, Hong Zhang

item.title: Spin-mediated modulation of chaos bound violation in Lorentz-violating black hole spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2607.21165v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate how the particle spin modulates chaos bound violations in Lorentz-violating black hole spacetimes within the framework of Bumblebee gravity. Using the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon formalism, we analyze the effects of spin-curvature coupling, Lorentz symmetry breaking, and the cosmological constant on the orbital instability in static spherically symmetric (A)dS black holes. We find that the particle spin provides an additional mechanism for modulating the critical angular momentum associated with the onset of violation. The Lorentz-violating parameter suppresses the violations by reducing the accessible parameter space and the critical charge. Meanwhile, a negative cosmological constant decreases the violation region but enhances the violation magnitude for allowed configurations. Our results demonstrate that the spin and Lorentz symmetry breaking jointly regulate the interplay between orbital instability and black hole horizon properties.
item.dc:creator: Chuang Yang, Deyou Chen, Bingbing Chen

item.title: Duru-Kleinert Path Integral in Unimodular Quantum Cosmology
item.description: arXiv:2608.18983v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Wheeler-DeWitt equation of a flat Friedmann-Lemaitre-Robertson-Walker universe filled with pressureless dust and a cosmological constant in unimodular gravity reduces, for a specific factor ordering and a specific self-adjoint extension, to the $l=0$ radial Schr\"odinger equation of a hydrogen atom. We revisit this correspondence from the point of view of the Green's functions and the Duru-Kleinert path integrals. Working directly with the reduced operator on the half-line, we obtain the Green's function in Whittaker form and fix its normalization by a Wronskian argument. Its Gamma-function poles give the reduced-operator spectrum which recovers the quantization of the negative cosmological term. We also perform the operator-level Duru-Kleinert transformation, whose Jacobian generates a barrier which after rescaling is exactly the centrifugal barrier of a two-dimensional oscillator. Retaining it reproduces the Coulomb pole condition. For positive cosmological constant, we give the continuum spectral measure and the Sommerfeld factor.
item.dc:creator: Xiao-Kan Guo

item.title: Spin-Inversion Degeneracies in Restricted Inspiral Waveforms for LISA
item.description: arXiv:2608.20174v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spin inversions appear in several settings. Analytical work predicts a single spin flip during unequal-mass supermassive binary inspiral, while numerical relativity and post-Newtonian calculations show repeated flip-flop motion in comparable-mass binaries. Secular spin evolution also predicts additional cases driven by spin-induced mass quadrupoles. Whether these effects can be distinguished in gravitational-wave data is still unclear. We combine the secular spin angle equations with a quasi-circular second post-Newtonian frequency evolution and build a restricted waveform weighted by the sky-averaged LISA sensitivity. We study five near-equal-mass injections with detector-frame total mass $M=2\times10^5M_\odot$, including Kerr flip-flops and one quadrupole-induced case. Each injection is compared with physically evolving waveforms constrained to have no orbital-plane crossings. We search all four no-inversion sectors, vary the masses, spin magnitudes, and initial spin angles, and maximize over time, phase, and overall amplitude. Large spin motion does not by itself lead to a clearly different waveform in this restricted model. We compare configurations with different spin magnitudes, relative spin orientations, and angular excursions at eleven observer inclinations between $0^\circ$ and $90^\circ$. With each injection normalized to signal SNR $\rho_\star=100$, four of the five cases leave a residual SNR below unity for the $0^\circ$ viewing direction along the total angular momentum. At nonzero inclinations, the residual associated with the largest match found reaches $7.07$ in the two-active-spin case at $55^\circ$. These upper bounds on the minimum residual within the allowed template family suggest potential distinguishability of spin inversions and motivate studies with more complete waveforms and the full LISA response.
item.dc:creator: Kata Kar\'acsonyi, L\'aszl\'o \'Arp\'ad Gergely

item.title: Gravitational-wave parameter estimation with machine-learning generated surrogate waveforms
item.description: arXiv:2608.20222v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The worldwide network of gravitational-wave detectors have detected more than 350 binary coalescence events till date. Future third-generation detectors, like Einstein telescope, are expected to detect orders-of-magnitude more signals from sources with more complicated characteristics, including eccentric orbits and high-mass ratio binaries. It is well-established that the computational cost of parameter estimation for signals from these kinds of sources will be extremely high. In particular, the process could be sped-up if generating theoretical waveform predictions, used for likelihood calculation becomes faster. Recently, various machine-learning techniques has been proposed to this end. In this work, we propose a two-stage deterministic conditional-autoencoder model for generating four-parameter SEOBNRv4 waveforms. The first-stage of the model generates amplitude and phase series of the waveform, while the second-stage calibrates the residual error in the predictions. Our model achieves a median mismatch of around $10^{-2}$ with the target polarization waveforms, while the calibrated amplitude/phase series achieve $10^{-6}$ level cosine distance error. We then propose a waveform conditioning step to enable use of these surrogate waveforms for downstream parameter estimation tasks. Finally, we perform extensive parameter estimation tests, with ML and EOB waveform injections and try to recover posterior estimates for the source parameters. We find that when ML waveforms are used to recover EOB target parameter estimates, the inferred posterior have some systematic bias. This inherent bias can be estimated and corrected for, and then importance reweighting of posterior samples can enable use of low-accuracy surrogate waveforms at low SNRs.
item.dc:creator: Suyog Garg, Kipp Cannon

item.title: Joule Thomson expansion of $\kappa$-deformed Schwarzschild-AdS black hole
item.description: arXiv:2608.22791v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the Joule-Thomson expansion of a non-commutative Schwarzschild-AdS black hole, whose space-time geometry is described by the Lie-algebraic $\kappa$-deformed space-time, and show that the $\kappa$-deformation parameter induces Joule-Thomson expansion in an uncharged-AdS black hole. We find the ratio of minimum inversion temperature to critical temperature $T_i^{(min)}/T_c \simeq 0.493$, is independent of the deformation parameter, and is in close agreement with the value for Reissner-Nordstrom black hole. Furthermore, we show the existence of a minimum black hole mass (depending on the $\kappa$-deformation parameter) below which the Joule-Thomson expansion vanishes.
item.dc:creator: Vishnu Rajagopal, Puxun Wu

item.title: Screened Scalar Hair and the Weak-Lensing Separation of Black Holes from Neutron Stars in Quadratic $f(R)$ Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2609.04419v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quadratic $f(R)$ gravity carries a massive scalar degree of freedom, the scalaron, whose finite range $\lambda$ screens its influence on the geometry outside a compact object. We show that this screening severs the exterior of a black hole from that of a neutron star of the same mass. Correction to the Schwarzschild metric is Yukawa-suppressed, falling as $e^{-r/\lambda}$ in the coupling, and is thus invisible to any expansion in powers of that coupling; the exterior is moreover intrinsically isotropic, so that inverting the temporal potential alone, as one does for single-potential solutions, fails to solve the field equations. Applying the Gibbons & Werner method of the Gauss-Bonnet theorem to this geometry, we find the leading deflection angle to be exactly the general-relativistic, ($b$: impact parameter), scalaron contributions cancelling identically in the combination that bends light. First correction carries the unfamiliar signature $\lambda^{-1/2}b^{-3/2}e^{-b/\lambda}$, screened beyond the scalaron range and confirmed against direct quadrature to around 20% at $b=4\lambda$, improving to 7% at $b=12\lambda$. What survives is the ingredients that deliver it, namely, non-analyticity in the coupling, the intrinsically isotropic gauge, the closed-form screened correction and the pressure-weighted scalar charge, are obtained within a single, self-consistent derivation here. A static black hole carries no scalar hair, and lenses precisely as general relativity requires; a neutron star acquires a scalar charge weighted by the pressure supporting it against collapse, and does not. Weak lensing therefore closes as a discriminant of the theory, whilst the horizon, as against a material surface, remains one in principle. The observational advantage lies in the strong-field imaging of the photon sphere, and in the stellar interior, where the scalar charge is fixed by the equation of state.
item.dc:creator: Yashmitha Kumaran, Il\'idio Lopes

item.title: Observational properties of magnetized quantum Oppenheimer-Snyder black holes
item.description: arXiv:2609.05906v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a thin accretion disk around the quantum Oppenheimer-Snyder black hole immersed in an asymptotically uniform magnetic field, together with the gravitational capture of test particles by the black hole. The field is described as a Wald test field and acts only on the weakly charged matter of the disk. We find that the quantum correction affects the disk only slightly, while the magnetic coupling strongly increases its radiative efficiency and luminosity and suppresses the Doppler blue peak of the iron K$\alpha$ line, which becomes a single peak below the rest frame energy. On the other hand, the quantum correction reduces all capture cross sections, while the magnetic field does not affect the capture of photons and confines charged particles to a finite region. Therefore, in principle, the two effects may be distinguished by combining spectral and shadow observations.
item.dc:creator: Anuar Idrissov, Hernando Quevedo

item.title: A computer assisted existence proof for a non-Schwarzschild black hole in Einstein--Weyl gravity
item.description: arXiv:2609.21797v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Static, asymptotically flat, non-Schwarzschild black holes in four-dimensional Einstein--Weyl gravity have previously been constructed by numerical shooting, while the local field equations admit horizon and asymptotic expansions to all orders. We give a computer assisted existence proof for a non-Schwarzschild solution whose dimensionless horizon radius is one in units of the massive spin-two scale, with parameters close to the previously reported numerical branch. The exterior is divided into a convergent horizon series domain, a compact core enclosed by a parameter dependent Taylor model with directed rounding, and an infinite asymptotic domain treated as a centered stable manifold fixed point problem. The resulting five-dimensional matching map between the core and tail is continuous on a rigorously specified box. After exact rational preconditioning, the signs on opposite faces satisfy the hypotheses of the Poincar\'e--Miranda theorem and therefore certify a matching zero. The solution has a regular nondegenerate horizon, no additional exterior horizon, vanishing Ricci scalar, and nonvanishing Ricci tensor. The strict bounds also imply existence at every sufficiently nearby horizon radius and a local continuous family at fixed coupling. The proof establishes existence, but not uniqueness of the matching zero.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Goldstein, Vishnu Jejjala

item.title: Axial Mode Stability and Quasinormal Modes of Charged Kiselev Black Holes in Rastall Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2609.25565v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate axial gravitoelectromagnetic perturbations of charged black holes surrounded by dust-like Kiselev-type anisotropic matter in Rastall gravity. We derive the axial matter compatibility condition and construct a compatible response by holding the covariant anisotropy-direction vector unperturbed. The resulting gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations obey two coupled Schrodinger-type master equations. An r-independent algebraic decoupling exists in the Reissner-Nordstrom and general-relativistic dust-like limits; additional radial structure obstructs it in generic charged Rastall backgrounds with nonzero surrounding matter. We prove axial mode stability under the adopted closure for every nonextremal background satisfying the stated exterior conditions, covering all physical axial multipoles. A matrix S-deformation excludes exponentially growing coupled modes for l >= 2, while the physical electromagnetic dipole has a positive effective potential. A Chebyshev pseudospectral calculation, validated against the Reissner-Nordstrom spectrum and spectral convergence, determines the fundamental frequencies. In the parameter ranges examined, increasing the Rastall coupling lowers both the oscillation frequency and the damping rate in the small-coupling region; in the large-coupling region, the oscillation frequency rises while the damping rate varies nonmonotonically. A larger charge generally raises the oscillation frequency, whereas stronger surrounding-matter contributions produce longer-lived modes.
item.dc:creator: Yan Wang, Yun-tao Gu, Wen-Di Guo

item.title: Closing the Loop: from EPRL-FK spinfoams to Regge dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2609.37179v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the semiclassical limit of the EPRL-FK model on a fixed simplicial complex. We ask what additional condition is needed for its variational principle to reproduce the equations of motion of Regge calculus, the standard discretization of General Relativity. This limit differs and complements the definition of the semiclassical regime in which, for suitable boundary states and a sufficiently refined simplicial complex, spinfoam amplitudes approximate gravitational transition amplitudes to a prescribed accuracy. We recast the EPRL-FK model in wedge-holonomy variables and identify geometric closure as the missing condition. We prove that imposing geometric closure as an additional constraint alongside local flatness allows us to reconstruct curved geometries. On a regular, nondegenerate Lorentzian branch with spacelike tetrahedra, these constraints define a surface equivalent to the space of length-Regge geometries, modulo gauge. The wedge action restricted to this surface becomes the Regge action, and variations tangent to this surface yield the length-Regge equations. We propose a way to implement geometric closure directly in the spinfoam amplitude. With this additional constraint, the EPRL-FK model is equivalent to Regge calculus in its semiclassical regime on a fixed simplicial complex.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Bruno, Pietro Don\`a, Gowrisankar Sreeram

item.title: MADGRAV: a multilevel anomaly-detection pipeline for gravitational-wave searches applied to LIGO data
item.description: arXiv:2609.39583v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present the results of \textbf{MADGRAV}, a deep-learning-based search for high-mass compact binary coalescences, applied to the data collected by the LIGO interferometers during the third observing run and during the first and second part of the fourth observing run. The \textbf{MADGRAV} pipeline consists of a series of sequential convolutional neural networks that perform anomaly detection, glitch classification, coherence testing, and signal ranking. Data from the Hanford and Livingston LIGO detectors are studied (both individually and in coherence) by way of 1 second Q-transform windows. Of the candidates that survive every stage of the pipeline, 48 reach the significance threshold, and we report 47 gravitational wave detections characterised by a false alarm rate below $1\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$ with a probability of astrophysical origin $p_{\rm astro}>0.9$. Of the 47 detections, 44 are shared with the minimally modelled coherent WaveBurst search. The observed total source-frame masses, extracted from official gravitational wave transient catalogues, are in the $14-236 M_{\odot}$ range with a median of $69 M_{\odot}$, and a median SNR of 16. We note that the recovered fraction of confident detections rises with mass: for LIGO detectors network SNR $>10$ the pipeline recovers $8.1\%$ of confident catalog events below $30 M_{\odot}$, $39.8\%$ between $30$ and $100 M_{\odot}$, and $53.3\%$ above $100 M_{\odot}$, corresponding to $33.3\%$, $45.5\%$ and $53.3\%$ of the events detected by coherent WaveBurst in the same bins. These results suggest that anomaly detection pipelines can serve as an independent detection channel complementary to matched filtering in the high-mass high-SNR regime.
item.dc:creator: Gianluca Inguglia, Huw Haigh, Ulyana Dupletsa, Alessandro Longo

item.title: Multi-Band Constraints on Cosmic Strings: Unifying Harmonic and Burst Spectra
item.description: arXiv:2610.02590v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Cosmic-string loops generate a broadband gravitational-wave background (GWB) that is typically modeled via two distinct formalisms: a discrete harmonic expansion, commonly used in pulsar-timing-array (PTA) studies, and a continuous burst superposition, employed in ground-based GWB searches. In this work, we formally unify the two formalisms, showing that they provide discrete and continuous representations of the same underlying radiation process and converge on the scale-invariant spectrum plateau. On the rising low-frequency branch, where the first few harmonics dominate, the discrete nature becomes important, causing the two formalisms to diverge. Within this unified framework, the spectral calculation is more consistent across frequency bands, enabling multi-band inference. Leveraging this physical insight, we perform joint Bayesian inference across four representative loop-distribution models using the NANOGrav, EPTA, and LIGO--Virgo--KAGRA (LVK) datasets. By jointly sampling the string tension $G\mu$ alongside the average cusp and kink numbers $\{N_c, N_k\}$, the loop-radiation uncertainties are accounted for. We find that employing the harmonic expansion strengthens the LVK bounds by $21\%-31\%$ for three of these models. Additionally, the stringent LVK bounds preclude three of these models from explaining the observed PTA common signal. For the sole surviving model, our multi-band analysis improves the inferred limit on $G\mu$.
item.dc:creator: Hansong Zhang, Huai-Ke Guo, Mairi Sakellariadou, Fengwei Yang, Yue Zhao

item.title: The efficiency gap of two-step forecasts for stochastic gravitational wave background searches
item.description: arXiv:2610.04459v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The stochastic gravitational-wave background is targeted by the millihertz observatories LISA, Taiji and TianQin, and its forecast precision rests on a Whittle approximation to the periodogram likelihood. The quoted scale is that of a joint fit a two-step forecast need not reach. We show that the residual risk of a two-step forecast lies in the estimator route rather than in the likelihood. At the exact Whittle form we separate the forecast error into a deterministic bias $\mathbf{b}$ and an efficiency gap $\mathbf{C}_b$, both in closed form. We find that this gap is governed by the span of the first-step nuisance fit. It decreases substantially as the span increases and vanishes when the first-step fit spans the entire band or when the response exhibits no within-bin structure. The gap does not arise as a cost of the prior. Across the LISA band the gap spans more than an order of magnitude, the amplitude and tilt inflation falling from about thirty and twenty to unity at a band-wide first step. A foreground from the released LDC2a population moves the mid-band gap by an order of magnitude. A two-step forecast should therefore report the span of its first-step fit with its intervals, since that span decides whether they sit at the Fisher scale or an order of magnitude above it.
item.dc:creator: Bo-Qiang Lu

item.title: Semiclassical Cosmological Constant in Anti-de Sitter and de Sitter Spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2610.09436v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the semiclassical Einstein equation for a quantized scalar field in four-dimensional anti-de Sitter (AdS) and de Sitter (dS) spacetimes. We first determine self-consistent configurations by fixing the bare cosmological constant to its geometric value, requiring the renormalized vacuum stress-energy tensor to vanish. In AdS, the resulting mass-curvature relations depend on the curvature coupling and boundary conditions; one formal Neumann root for minimal coupling is excluded by the admissible parameter range, whereas both Dirichlet and Neumann solutions are allowed for conformal coupling. In dS, we recover the known self-consistent solution for a minimally coupled massive field. We then evaluate the effective cosmological constant on prescribed backgrounds in four massless configurations. In each case, it takes the form \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{eff}}=A/\ell^2+B/\ell^4\). The competition between classical curvature and vacuum polarization produces a minimum and a zero in the minimally coupled AdS case, while the other configurations are monotonic. Finally, the formal continuation \(\ell\rightarrow i\ell\) fails to reproduce the directly calculated quantum coefficients: their AdS-to-dS ratios are \(29/61\) for minimal coupling and \(-1\) for conformal coupling. These results show that continuation of the curvature scale alone does not establish equivalence between the semiclassical vacuum contributions in AdS and dS.
item.dc:creator: Milton C. Mamani-Leqque

item.title: Separation of variables for coupled radiative perturbations of Kerr-Newman-de Sitter black holes
item.description: arXiv:2610.20500v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend Hintz's separation of variables for radiative gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations from Kerr-Newman to Kerr-Newman-de Sitter black holes. On subextremal backgrounds with nonzero rotation and charge, an explicit algebraic matrix transformation yields coupled two-component radial and angular ordinary differential systems linked by a common separation constant. The transformation is independent of the frequency and azimuthal number and applies to both signs of spin weight. For real frequencies, we establish a complete angular mode decomposition. We also translate regularity at the future black hole outer and cosmological horizons into ingoing and outgoing boundary conditions, respectively, for the separated radial systems. These results show that exact separation of the coupled radiative equations extends beyond asymptotically flat Kerr-Newman spacetime.
item.dc:creator: Daisuke Yoshida

item.title: Quantum superposition of black hole states as a communication resource
item.description: arXiv:2203.05861v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The interplay between black holes and quantum information has revealed deep connections between gravity and quantum mechanics. For example, the classical spacetime geometry of a black hole has been shown to degrade quantum entanglement shared by nearby observers, one of whom is in free fall. Here we examine how this picture changes when the black hole's mass degrees of freedom are allowed to exist in a coherent quantum superposition, corresponding to a superposition of distinct spacetime geometries. We show that such quantum coherence can mitigate the loss of entanglement between nearby observers, thereby enhancing the performance of quantum communication protocols operating in the vicinity of the black hole.
item.dc:creator: Richard Howl, Ali Akil, Hl\'er Kristj\'ansson, Xiaobin Zhao, Giulio Chiribella

item.title: Gravitational waves from cosmic superstrings and gauge strings
item.description: arXiv:2312.10455v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We perform a phenomenological comparison of the gravitational wave (GW) spectrum expected from cosmic gauge string networks and superstring networks comprised of multiple string types. We show how violations of scaling behavior and the evolution of the number of relativistic degrees of freedom in the early Universe affect the GW spectrum. We derive simple analytical expressions for the GW spectrum from superstrings and gauge strings that are valid for all frequencies relevant to pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) and laser interferometers. We analyze the latest data from PTAs and show that superstring networks are consistent with 32 nHz data from NANOGrav, but are excluded by 3.2 nHz data at $3\sigma$ unless the string coupling $g_s<0.2$ or the strings evolve in only about 10% of the volume of the higher-dimensional space. We also point out that while gauge string networks are excluded by NANOGrav-15 data at $3\sigma$, they are completely compatible with EPTA and PPTA data. Finally, we study correlations between GW signals at PTAs and laser interferometers.
item.dc:creator: Danny Marfatia, Ye-Ling Zhou

item.title: Rethinking Symmetry Principles and Partial Observables With Reference Frames
item.description: arXiv:2410.12892v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Dynamically uncoupled fields are a modelling device used in the literature on reference frames, classical and quantum. We argue that the device is not innocuous. First, uncoupled fields violate Earman's symmetry principle SP1---that every dynamical symmetry is a spacetime symmetry---and the violation, unlike the familiar Newtonian one, cannot be repaired by excising surplus spacetime structure: it arises from a deficit of dynamical structure, not an excess of spatiotemporal structure. This qualifies implicit assumptions of Earman's SP1, while leaving its diagnostic role intact. Second, uncoupled fields expose a lacuna in the partial/complete observables programme: only dynamically coupled fields can serve as bona-fide partial observables, so partial observability is derivative on complete observability. We then reinterpret the standard formalism for partial observables: qua measurable, a partial observable is a relational quantity expressed with respect to an uncoupled frame, and it remains gauge-variant. This reinterpretation vindicates Rovelli's claim that partial observables are individually measurable, against Thiemann and Adlam, and separates two properties easily conflated in the generally covariant formulations of theories: invariance under diffeomorphisms and invariance along the gauge flow.
item.dc:creator: Nicola Bamonti, Henrique Gomes

item.title: Cosmological pole-skipping, shock waves and quantum chaotic dynamics of de Sitter horizons
item.description: arXiv:2508.15589v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a systematic analysis of pole-skipping for scalar, Maxwell, and gravitational waves in cosmological spacetimes. Specifically, working in empty de Sitter space and in Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole geometries, we locate the tower of pole-skipping points of such fields and show that they impose nontrivial constraints on the corresponding bulk two-point functions. Focusing on the gravitational sound channel, we then extract the Lyapunov exponent and butterfly velocities that characterize hypothetical dual many-body quantum chaos at each horizon. These chaotic data precisely match the outcome of a gravitational shock wave calculation, confirming that the relevant pole-skipping points encode high-energy scattering of horizon quanta. Interestingly, the butterfly velocities can become superluminal or imaginary, with the latter signaling a spatially modulated propagation of chaos. Assuming that a holographic dual exists, we translate our results into field theory language and propose that the dual theory can be divided into two entangled sectors that capture the black hole and cosmological horizon degrees of freedom. Our results suggest that the black hole sector becomes increasingly nonlocal as the black hole shrinks and that the cosmological horizon sector exhibits behavior compatible with violations of Hermiticity. Finally, we outline simple microscopic toy models, built from long-range and non-Hermitian deformations of the Double Scaled Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (DSSYK)-type chains, that realize these features, providing a concrete arena for future exploration.
item.dc:creator: Yongjun Ahn, Sa\v{s}o Grozdanov, Hyun-Sik Jeong, Juan F. Pedraza

item.title: The relativistic reason for quantum probability amplitudes
item.description: arXiv:2512.10497v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that the quantum-mechanical probability distribution involving complex probability amplitudes can be derived from three natural conditions imposed on a relativistically invariant probability function describing the motion of a particle that can take multiple paths simultaneously. The conditions are: (i) pairwise Kolmogorov additivity, (ii) time symmetry, and (iii) Bayes' rule. The resulting solution, parameterized by a single constant, is the squared modulus of a sum of complex exponentials of the relativistic action, thereby recovering the Feynman path-integral formulation of quantum mechanics.
item.dc:creator: Karol Sajnok, Kacper D\k{e}bski, Andrzej Dragan
